# Policy grammar

Every construct the policy parser accepts, each in brief. The file is regenerated whenever the
language changes, so it matches what compiles. The checker is still the judge: check every draft
with `scripts/check.py`.

```text
GRAMMAR (every construct below is accepted by the parser; [x] marks x optional):

A document is one `policy { ... }` block containing, in any order:

  role <name>
  action <name>(<param>: <type>, ...)      // types: bool int amount text party role tick action transaction
  party <name> principal
  party <name> agent [roles(<role>, ...)]
  delegation <name> {
    principal <party>
    agent <party>
    scope { actions(<action>, ...) roles(<role>, ...) [window(<start>, <end>)] }
  }
  aggregate <name> counts <action> <scope> over <window>
  aggregate <name> sums <action>(<param>) <scope> over <window> [in <CUR>]
  aggregate <name> sums posted [debit|credit] <CUR> [in <account>] <action> <scope> over <window>
  rule <name> {
    <modality> <actor> do <action> [{ <param>: <value>, ... }]   // modality: permitted | obligated | forbidden
    trigger <action> [{ <param>: <value>, ... }]        // optional; obligations only
    capture { <param>: trigger_param(<param>) | trigger_transaction, ... }   // optional; obligations only
    performed_by debtor | trigger_party(<param>) | specific(<party>)         // optional; obligations only
    when { <clause> and <clause> ... }       // optional guard (CNF); each clause: ( <literal> or <literal> ... )
    within(<n>) | by(<tick>) | during(<start>, <end>)   // optional temporal bound
    unless <name> { <clause> ... }           // optional named defeater (a firing defeater outranks this rule)
    on_violation <rule>                       // optional; obligations only; names a reparation rule
    priority <n>                              // required on every rule
  }

  <scope>    ::= per party | per role <role> | per counterparty(<param>) [within each mandate root]
               | per rail <rail> | global
  <window>   ::= rolling <ticks> | calendar <ticks> | unbounded
  <actor>    ::= any_in_role(<role>) | specific(<party>)
  <literal>  ::= [not] <term> <op> <term>
  <term>     ::= param(<name>) | actor | now | <value>
               | spent(<mandate>) | ceiling(<mandate>) | remaining(<mandate>) | projected(<mandate>)
               | register(<name>) | projected(register(<name>))
               | counterparty limit(<param>)             // right-hand side of a comparison only
               | resolved counterparty(<param>)          // compare with == != or in only
               | posted [debit|credit] <CUR> [in <account>]
  <op>       ::= == != < <= > >= in
  <value>    ::= bool(true|false) | int(<n>) | amount(<minor>, <CUR>) | text("...")
               | party(<name>) | role(<name>) | tick(<n>) | action(<name>) | transaction(<txn_id>)
  reference sets (right-hand side of `in` only):
               param(<x>) in approved counterparties   // x is a text or party param
               param(<x>) in chart of accounts          // x is a text or party param
               param(<x>) in open fiscal periods        // x is a tick param

RULES OF THE LANGUAGE:
  - Comments are `//` to end of line. Names use [a-z0-9_], 1-64 bytes.
  - Amounts are integer minor units plus a currency code of 3 to 8 uppercase letters (ISO-4217, or a
    stablecoin ticker such as USDC), e.g. amount(50000, USD) is $500.00.
  - Never compare two amounts of different currencies.
  - `on_violation`, `trigger`, `capture` and `performed_by` may appear only on `obligated` rules;
    every clause but `unless` comes at most once per rule. `capture` fills the owed action's
    parameters from the action that triggered the duty (`trigger_param(<param>)`) or with that
    action's transaction id (`trigger_transaction`, into a `transaction` parameter). `performed_by`
    names who may perform the duty: the obligated party (`debtor`, the default), the party a `party`
    parameter of the trigger named (`trigger_party(<param>)`), or a declared party
    (`specific(<party>)`).
  - A duty with no `trigger` is opened by a committed proposal of its own action; when the proposer
    performs it and every `capture` copies a parameter into itself, that same proposal discharges it,
    so a `within` deadline never lapses. When missing a deadline should open an `on_violation`
    reparation, give the duty a `trigger` (the action that opens it) and a `within` or `by` deadline.
    When another party performs it (`performed_by`), or a `capture` takes another parameter's value
    or the transaction id (`trigger_transaction`), it can stay open, and only a `within` or `by`
    deadline lets it lapse and open its `on_violation`. A `when` conjunct `( param(n) == param(m) )`
    counts a capture of `m` into `n` as a copy, and `( param(p) == actor )` makes a
    `trigger_party(p)` performer the proposer; a guard that forces the values equal any other way is
    not read.
  - A reparation (an obligation an `on_violation` names, with no `trigger`) opens only on that breach,
    and on every one: the breach reads none of its `when`, `unless` or `during`, so the checker refuses
    them there (DSL0032). Give it its own `within` (counted from the breach) or `by` deadline, or it
    never lapses and its own `on_violation` never fires.
  - Every role, action, and party a rule or scope names must be declared in the same policy. A
    `specific(<party>)` that names no declared party selects only a party bound under that name at run
    time, so a misspelled one governs nobody.
  - A guard predicate may only reference params declared on the rule's action (or its trigger).
  - An aggregate's action must be declared; `sums` targets an int- or amount-typed parameter.
  - An aggregate that sums an amount-typed parameter must end with `in <CUR>`; no other aggregate takes `in <CUR>`.
  - Compare `register(<name>)` against a constant of its value type (a count reads as int, a sum as its parameter's type).
  - Compare a mandate term with < <= > or >= only, against an amount(...); `projected(m)` alone may instead be
    compared with that same mandate's ceiling, e.g. `projected(buyer_mandate) > ceiling(buyer_mandate)`. A param,
    spent, remaining, projected, another mandate's ceiling and a register are never on a mandate term's right, and
    spent, remaining or ceiling is never compared with a ceiling. An amount(...) cap is written in the mandate's own
    currency, never another, so every cap on one mandate, unless clauses included, is in one currency.
    `projected(m)` counts this transaction when it is charged to m or to a mandate carved from m.
  - There is exactly one way to write each construct; do not invent keywords or operators.

CONVENTIONS CALLERS DEPEND ON:
  - A policy for agents that pay through the SDK's one-call `authorize` declares exactly
    `action purchase(amount: amount, payee: text)`: that is the action and the parameter
    types the SDK proposes. A payment rail binds `payee` as `party` unless its operator set
    `payee_binding = "text"`; declare `payee: party` only for a rail left on `party`.
  - A rule or aggregate that scopes by `counterparty(payee)` needs every payee imported
    into the counterparty registry. An unregistered payee is rejected before judgment, not
    refused; import it with `approved: false` to have it refused.

```
